title: Pedestrian crossing and safe states
summary: Walk through pedestrian-crossing states with mutually consistent vehicle and pedestrian outputs.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Model the crossing as numbered states, each with an explicit output combination.
Show WALK only while the vehicles are red.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/PedestrianCrossing.st, add the states that coordinate vehicles and pedestrians; the plant raises PedRequest from {{t:10}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: Each state must leave an explicit output combination.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict the light and pedestrian-signal sequence.
stages.checkpoint: green+STOP {{t:0}} ms; yellow+STOP {{t:20}}; red+STOP {{t:40}}; red+WALK {{t:60}}; red+STOP {{t:90}}; green+STOP {{t:110}}.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}: The starter ignores the pedestrian request; after PedRequest run yellow, red clearance, WALK, and red recovery before returning to green, and show WALK only while the vehicles are red.
stages.checkpoint: Check reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named PedestrianCrossing and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Review the recorded matrix in Tests and compare every sample with the prediction.
stages.checkpoint: The trace shows WALK only during the red state.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The NEVER assertion covers logically incompatible outputs only in this scenario.
stages.checkpoint: What the assertions check is tested; nothing else is.

hints.text: Keep one State variable and one counter of scans; at the top of every scan set all outputs to the safe default (vehicles stopped, pedestrians told to wait) and let each state turn on only what it needs.
The sequence is green, yellow, red clearance, WALK, red recovery, then green again; leave green only on PedRequest and move to the next state when the scan counter reaches that phase's length.

faultCases: The starter ignores the pedestrian request; after PedRequest run yellow, red clearance, WALK, and red recovery before returning to green, and show WALK only while the vehicles are red.
